scope: Bounded local model two-pass single-card review; not independent human approval.

cards.title: First to Solve It
cards.instruction: Treat each clue and inconsistency as a contest over who can understand the situation first and most completely.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've found the missing parcel's tracking error. Put my name beside it.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We were both looking.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I circled it while you were saying looking.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Let's fix it together.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: After recording who made together useful.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've solved your missing parcel. Tracking says reception; you were still refreshing.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Reception signed for three boxes. Only two reached our office.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then one stayed downstairs. I've narrowed your whole building to one desk.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The trolley's here. There's a box wedged underneath.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: So it left reception but never got unloaded. You've found the parcel; I've solved why we've been calling reception all morning.

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 and A3 claim credit for an error, but A5 prioritizes recording credit over understanding more completely.

responseLogic.evidence: A3 counters B2's shared search; A5 makes B4's cooperative fix conditional on attribution.

relationship.evidence: B2 claims joint effort and B4 offers practical cooperation that A obstructs.

heightening.evidence: A5 repeats the credit demand without introducing another clue or a more complete explanation.

specificity.evidence: A1 establishes a missing parcel's tracking error and an immediate attribution dispute.

brevityWit.evidence: A3's circled-versus-looking line fits rivalry; A5's together-useful phrasing becomes abstract.

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 contrasts A's claimed solution with B 'still refreshing'; A3 claims superior narrowing; A5 counters B's discovery by claiming the more complete explanation. Competitive understanding is clear, though A3's certainty outruns the evidence.

responseLogic.evidence: B2's three-box receipt and two-box arrival cause A3's downstairs hypothesis. B4's box under the trolley overturns that hypothesis, and A5 incorporates it into an unloading explanation while reclaiming credit.

relationship.evidence: B2 contributes delivery facts and B4 actually finds the box, pursuing parcel recovery rather than merely feeding boasts. A5 acknowledges B's achievement while competing over what counts as solving.

heightening.evidence: After B4 wins the physical search, A5 raises the contest from locating the parcel to explaining the morning's wasted calls. This develops the established competition, though chiefly through a verbal claim.

specificity.evidence: A1 immediately establishes parcel tracking and reception; B2 supplies the three-versus-two discrepancy; B4 reveals the box wedged under the trolley. Each detail gives actors a clear, playable discovery.

brevityWit.evidence: A3's 'one desk' makes premature certainty compactly comic. A5's distinction between finding and solving follows B4, although the final explanation is longer and more explicit than the earlier boasts.

hardGateEvidence.b2CausesA3: B2 establishes a box missing between reception and the office; A3 uses that discrepancy to claim it stayed downstairs.
hardGateEvidence.b4CausesA5: B4 locates the box under the trolley, forcing A5 to abandon the downstairs claim and compete instead over explaining why it remained missing.
hardGateEvidence.cardContribution: A1, A3 and A5 repeatedly turn parcel evidence into claims of intellectual precedence or completeness, directed at the colleague making competing discoveries.
hardGateEvidence.sameGameHeightened: A5 responds to losing the search by claiming a broader explanatory victory. Finding the parcel resolves a fictional problem without prescribing an ending for the actual scene.

mechanismDistinction.mechanism: A treats understanding each clue first and extending that understanding furthest as a competition.
mechanismDistinction.confusableConcept: Credit seeking wants recognition for a contribution; this card makes continuing interpretation itself the race.
mechanismDistinction.distinguishingEvidenceRequired: Revised A3 interprets B2's unequal box counts as a location; A5 uses B4's trapped box to replace that theory with a failed-unloading explanation and claim fuller understanding than B's discovery.

records.recommendedEdit: Preserved the original firstPass exactly. Kept the office parcel search, replacing the date and proposed speakerphone race with box counts and a trolley carrying the missing box. The rejected A5 only promised understanding; the new B4 supplies physical evidence that A5 immediately uses to explain the failed delivery while maintaining superiority. Separate internal reread under coach-1.0: fidelity 5 (A1 races B's refreshing; A5 claims explanation outranks discovery), logic 4 (B2's count supports A3's hasty location theory; B4's trapped box supports A5's unloading explanation), relationship 4 (B2 contributes the delivery discrepancy and B4 actively finds the box), heightening 4 (A5 absorbs the correction by expanding location into a causal account), specificity 4 (A1 tracking, B2 office delivery, B4 trolley), brevity 4 (A5's found/solved distinction follows the evidence): 86. Five spoken ABABA turns, 74 words, and causal gates pass. Separate internal model reread only; the transfer reservation remains unresolved.
records.remainingConcern: A3 makes an unsupported deduction, and A5's explanatory victory is slight because B4 has supplied the decisive evidence. These remain playable expressions of sincere competitive certainty. No rewrite is needed.
records.writerReservation: A3 mistakes an unaccounted-for box for proof it stayed downstairs; A5 also assumes the wedged box is their parcel before checking its label. These are visible competitive overclaims, and B remains free to correct them. The final line adds the morning's calls as shared search history.
records.alternativeComparison: The preserved S130-single-b has B challenge successive mystery-judge deductions while A claims the fuller sequence. Here B independently recovers a real missing item, forcing A to concede the discovery and shift the criterion for victory to explanation.

cards.title: First to Solve It
cards.instruction: Treat each clue and inconsistency as a contest over who can understand the situation first and most completely.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: The mystery guest is the baker. I solved it.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I told you about the flour.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: A clue is not a conclusion.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I said it was the baker.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Yes, but I believed it decisively.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Our mystery judge is the baker. Flour on the invitation. Solved before you.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The miller uses flour too.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then it's the miller. I've already moved past the obvious answer.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: There's icing on the envelope flap.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: The baker, licking it after decorating. I've got the identity and the sequence; you've got ingredients.

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 declares a solved mystery, but A5 replaces being first or most complete with a claim to decisive belief.

responseLogic.evidence: A3 distinguishes B2's clue from a conclusion; B4 removes that defense and A5 invents a new one.

relationship.evidence: B2 claims the clue and B4 credibly corrects A's account of who named the baker.

heightening.evidence: A5 intensifies the self-serving claim but stops advancing understanding of the mystery.

specificity.evidence: A1 supplies a mystery guest and B2 flour, without establishing the occasion.

brevityWit.evidence: A5's decisive belief is a compact response to B4, though it rewards credit grabbing over deduction.

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 claims 'Solved before you'; A3 claims to be ahead despite changing answers; A5 contests completeness of understanding.

responseLogic.evidence: B2's miller possibility causes A3's switch; B4's icing causes A5 to return to the baker with an added sequence.

relationship.evidence: B2 challenges an inference and B4 supplies discriminating evidence, repeatedly threatening A's claim to superiority.

heightening.evidence: A5 responds to B4's better clue by claiming both identity and chronology, then reducing B's contribution to ingredients.

specificity.evidence: A1 establishes a mystery judge and flour on an invitation; B4 locates icing on the envelope flap.

brevityWit.evidence: A5's 'identity and the sequence' versus 'ingredients' turns B's useful clue into A's competitive accounting.

hardGateEvidence.b2CausesA3: B2 identifies another flour user; A3 adopts that suspect while claiming the change demonstrates being ahead.
hardGateEvidence.b4CausesA5: B4 adds icing on the flap; A5 restores the baker and invents a more complete account to reclaim superiority.
hardGateEvidence.cardContribution: A treats every clue as a contest for first and fullest understanding, including evidence supplied by B.
hardGateEvidence.sameGameHeightened: A shifts the competition from naming the judge first to claiming the entire sequence of events.

mechanismDistinction.mechanism: A turns every clue and correction into a contest to reach the earliest and most complete explanation.
mechanismDistinction.confusableConcept: Professional suspicion delays action to investigate; competitive solving uses investigation to outrank another person's understanding.
mechanismDistinction.distinguishingEvidenceRequired: Revised A1 explicitly races B, and A5 claims both identity and sequence as superior to B's isolated clue.

records.recommendedEdit: Added a mystery-judge invitation while retaining baker and flour. Separate reread: fidelity 5 (A1 firstness and A5 completeness), logic 5 (B2 miller revises A3; B4 icing revises A5), relationship 4 (B contributes rival evidence), heightening 4 (A5 claims a sequence), specificity 4 (A1 invitation), brevity 4 (A5 ingredients comparison): 90. All dialogue gates pass.
records.remainingConcern: The licking-and-decorating sequence is speculative, but reads as A's competitive overclaim rather than an established deduction. No rewrite needed.
records.writerReservation: A's deductions remain overconfident: icing suggests a baker but cannot prove the proposed licking sequence.
records.alternativeComparison: Alternative b has an active evidentiary rival and explicit credit competition; a relies on cooperative confirmation and unexplained knowledge.
